newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease, but rise seen on back of Dow.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease, but rise seen on back of Dow.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased on Wednesday, but traders said they expected the market to firm on Thursday due to U.S. economic data which analysts said could make a U.S. interest rate hike less likely.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed lower at 349.75 on a healthy $41.9 million total market volume. The RTS closed on Tuesday at 353.99.

"I'm very optimistic about tomorrow -- some very good figures on the American economy came out today which could have the power to lift the mood of market operators," said senior United City Bank trader Samit Yakovlev.
"Of course, there is not a direct correlation between them and Russian share prices but the closer we get to May 20, the more those kind of things affect the market."
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee is due to meet on May 20, and investors are worried it could raise interest rates again if the economy looks overheated.
"Many of our people are looking at the Dow Jones right now and we're staking our hopes on those people," said MFK-Moscow Partners trader Ivan Deryabin.
Traders said the market's weakness on Wednesday was due to sales by regional operators who failed to react to Wall Street's news.
But demand was strong from both domestic and Western investors for leading shares as well as for second-tier, less liquid stock, they said.
UCB's Yakovlev said oil companies Surgutneftegaz and LUKoil saw the biggest demand of the market "blue chips".

He that LUKoil's plans, announced after market close on Tuesday, to seek authorisation for 10 million new preferred shares were not scaring investors off, as demand was already soaking up big packets of shares from a number of large firms.
LUKoil, Russia's largest oil producer eased to $14.70 from Tuesday's closing $14.74, while Surgutneftegaz slipped to $0.878 from $0.890. But market leader UES firmed up to $0.3000 from $0.2975.
MFK's Deryabin said Kolenergo and Rostovenergo were in demand among less liquid shares.
Kolenergo firmed to $0.305 from $0.299 on Tuesday, while Rostovenergo, which trades on RTS-2, slipped to $0.0900 from $0.0911.
